note: The archetype slot registry (FORMAT-SPEC §7). Every gameplay asset fills a core slot and supplies the numbers that slot defines; core owns the field list, and a pack that invents a field gets a warning and has it ignored. The point is that a slot is a promise about behaviour: anything in `ranged_slow` is aimed, cycled and reloaded by the same core code whether it is a musket, a bolt rifle or a crossbow.
status: Reviewed at C4 (2026-07-31), which BUILD-ORDER carried over from C1 for the reason it gave: only the prop slots had been exercised, so until weapons existed a review was about words rather than numbers. Three slots added — `signalling`, `optics`, `utility` — all of which CHECKLIST §4 had asked for and none of which existed. **`entrenching` was asked for and deliberately not added**; see `DEVIATIONS-C4.md` B6. Now 29 slots. Expect this list to be argued with again once vehicles and emplacements carry real numbers, which is C6.

ranged_slow.note: bolt rifle, musket, crossbow, bow — one deliberate shot at a time

ranged_fast.note: submachine gun, automatic rifle — volume over placement

ranged_support.note: machine gun, crew-served — sited rather than carried into a fight

ranged_precision.note: scoped rifle — the slot exists so optics are core behaviour, not a stat

sidearm.note: pistol, revolver — a fallback, not a primary

melee_light.note: knife, shortsword, entrenching tool — fast, and `dig_cm` is what makes the last of those a tool as well as a weapon

melee_heavy.note: polearm, two-hander, sledge, pick — slow, and it moves the target; `dig_cm` covers the pick, which digs harder and swings slower than a spade

explosive_launched.note: mortar, rocket, hand cannon — indirect or shoulder-fired

heavy_transport.note: truck, limber, barge — logistics rather than a fight

armoured_fighting.note: tank, armoured car. `health` is the crew-and-systems pool, not the plating — the plating is a material

mount.note: the horse. A mount is a vehicle with a gait — RIG-SPEC §1 is the whole reason this slot is in the first cut

gun_fixed.note: a gun that is part of the terrain — bunker gun, turret

gun_crewed.note: field gun, siege engine — it takes people to work it

observation.note: periscope, spotting scope, forward observer post

barrier.note: sandbag wall, gabion, hesco. No health — durability comes from the material it is built of

span.note: duckboard, bridge, ladder — the things that make ground crossable

infantry.note: core owns a soldier's movement and health, so a class asset is a loadout and a silhouette rather than a stat block

specialist.note: sapper, medic, engineer — the tool is what makes the class

signalling.note: whistle, horn, flare pistol, signal lamp — a thing whose whole output is being noticed. `carry_range` is how far the signal itself travels, which is the only stat that matters and is not the same question as a weapon's range

optics.note: binoculars, trench periscope, rangefinder — held rather than emplaced, which is what makes it a different slot from `observation`. Requires only `zoom`: an optic that does not magnify is a prop

utility.note: wire cutters, wrench, dressing, demolition charge — the kit that is carried in a weapon slot and is not for hitting anyone. `work_power` is the tool-gating number MATERIAL-SPEC uses, so a pair of cutters can be refused by armour plate with a reason
